root_cause: Spec/ADR T-0588 (docs/specs/T-0588-substitution-escalation.spec.md, docs/design/T-0588.adr.md) documented two structural read-path gaps, neither requiring a new data model. (1) Claim-eligibility gap: POST /api/inbox/:id/claim gated eligibility strictly on role_assignment (resolveRolesForActor -> getRoleSlugsForActor); a Tier-2 substitute (substitution_rule.ttl_grant_id SET -- a TTL'd grant, NOT a role_assignment) got 403 NOT_ELIGIBLE despite an effective, confirmed, in-window rule. (2) Deactivation gap: getHoldersForRole and findTenantOwnerSlug (grants-dao.ts) JOIN employee but never filtered deactivated_at IS NULL, so a fired employee stayed in the role holder pool and could still resolve as fallback-owner -- new tasks would silently pile up on an account that can no longer log into Keycloak.

fix_summary.claim_eligibility_tier2: src/http/inbox.ts POST /api/inbox/:id/claim: after the existing taskRole-in-myRoles check fails, an ADDITIVE branch consults getActiveSubstitutionsForSubstitute(pool, tenantId, actorSlug, nowMs) (new DAO reader). Matches require roleId===taskRole, ttlGrantId!==null (Tier-2 only -- a Tier-1 substitute already holds the role via role_assignment and passes the existing check), isRuleEffective(rule, nowMs) (confirmed_by NOT NULL + in-window), and isNarrowerOrEqual(taskOrgScope=BOTTOM, rule.orgScope, NO_OP ancestry) -- mirroring resolveExecutor's default org-scope handling. On a match the claim is allowed and the absent holder's slug flows through to appendTaskClaimed as onBehalfOf. The branch is local to the claim endpoint only -- getRoleSlugsForActor/myRoles are untouched (per ADR's rejected-alternatives: widening myRoles would leak substituted authority into the approve path and other role-slug consumers).
fix_summary.on_behalf_of_provenance: src/http/claim-projection.ts appendTaskClaimed gains an OPTIONAL onBehalfOf?: string arg. When set, the task.claimed audit_event payload gains an on_behalf_of key (JSONB, free-form) recording the absent holder's slug. When omitted (normal role-assignment claim), the payload key is omitted entirely -- byte-identical to the pre-T-0588 shape. Per ADR: on_behalf_of lives in the JSONB payload, NOT a new column, because audit_event's column set feeds the hash-chain preimage and audit_event has no on_behalf_of column at all (that lives on the separate actor_event table, migration 018, unrelated SoD ledger) -- zero migration, zero preimage change.
fix_summary.deactivation_filter: src/db/grants-dao.ts: added `AND e.deactivated_at IS NULL` to getHoldersForRole, findTenantOwnerSlug, findTenantOwnerEmployeeId, and getAuthoringDraftHolderEmployeeIds (the last two for consistency -- a deactivated owner should not be a config-request notification recipient either, per ADR rejected-alternatives). All four signatures and return shapes are UNCHANGED -- purely an additive SQL predicate. A deactivated employee now never appears as a role holder and never resolves as fallback-owner.
fix_summary.escalation_falls_out_free: FR-3/FR-4 required no new code: resolveExecutorFallbackBatch (path B, src/http/inbox.ts) already reads getHoldersForRole/findTenantOwnerSlug for its suppress-absent + substitute + fallback ladder -- once those DAO functions exclude deactivated employees, a deactivated sole holder with an active Tier-1 substitution_rule routes to the substitute automatically, and a deactivated holder with no substitution_rule (and an active owner) routes to routed_to_fallback:'role_unfilled' automatically. resolveExecutor (path A, pure) already returns kind:'unresolvable' when the injected fallback port returns null (now the DB-backed reality once the owner is also deactivated) -- covered by a new pure unit test, not new production code.
fix_summary.path_a_not_wired: Per FR-5/ADR, resolveExecutor (path A) is confirmed by reconnaissance to have zero production write/read callers -- production routing runs through resolveExecutorFallbackBatch (path B) plus the claim endpoint. No composition-root wiring of ResolverDeps.substitution was added; doing so would be dead code for this slice and risk a second, divergent routing authority (ND-3, tech-debt follow-up, explicitly out of scope).

friction_events: Initial misuse of core resolveSubstitution(rules, employeeId, roleId, orgScope, ancestry, nowMs) in the claim route: its employeeId parameter expects the ALREADY-KNOWN absent holder, which the claim endpoint does not have in advance (it only knows the actor/substitute and taskRole). Caught before committing by re-reading src/core/substitution.ts's actual signature; fixed by filtering the getActiveSubstitutionsForSubstitute result directly with isRuleEffective + isNarrowerOrEqual (both already-exported pure helpers) instead of forcing resolveSubstitution's mismatched shape onto this call site. No wasted commit -- caught in the same edit pass via tsc, before any test run.

First iteration of the new db test file (inbox_claim_substitution.db.test.ts) seeded via the appPool (choros_app, RLS-enforced) connection for choros.tenant INSERT, which the tenant table's RLS policy rejects for non-BYPASSRLS roles -- 'new row violates row-level security policy for table tenant'. Fixed by switching all seeding in that file to a migratorUrl() (BYPASSRLS) connection, matching the established pattern in ci/checks/db/grants-dao-dual-control.db.test.ts. A second, related fix: appendProcessStarted (called on the same migrator connection to seed the pool task) reads the tenant id via `current_setting('choros.tenant_id', false)` inside appendAuditEvent -- this GUC is not automatically set on a BYPASSRLS connection, so an explicit `SET LOCAL choros.tenant_id = '<tenantId>'` was added right after each transaction's BEGIN.

Test assertions initially checked JSON.parse(resp.body).code for the 403 NOT_ELIGIBLE case; the router's actual error envelope is { error: { code, message } } (src/http/router.ts), not a bare { code }. Fixed by reading .error.code -- caught immediately by the first db-test run (AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'NOT_ELIGIBLE'), not discovered later.
